pool.text: Norman lord Robert D'Oyly built Oxford Castle to secure control of the area.
Scholars fled Oxford and founded Cambridge University following a dispute with the town.
The Scholastica Day Riot lasted days and caused numerous student and townsperson deaths.
The theologian John Wycliffe was expelled from the University of Oxford
Oxford was granted city status when the Diocese of Oxford was created.
The long-established independent retailer Boswells was founded on Cornmarket Street and Queen Street.
Hall's Brewery was acquired by Samuel Allsopp and Sons, ending its brewing in Oxford.
Oxford Cheetahs motorcycle speedway team has raced at Oxford Stadium in Cowley
Greyhound racing took place at the Oxford Stadium until a later closure date
The Oxfordshire and Buckinghamshire Light Infantry established a specific military date entry
The 1st Green Jackets (43rd and 52nd) formed on a specific date
A hurling club was originally founded by Irish immigrants in this year
Daily Information began publishing as a local event information and advertising news sheet.
A dual carriageway section featuring two residential service roads on the A40 was completed.
The Royal Green Jackets established their official organizational date
The M40 motorway approached Oxford, leading from London to Waterstock where the A40 continued.
The Saints were founded as one of the longest-running American football clubs
The Oxford Cheetahs became British League champions during a successful decade
The Oxford Cheetahs secured another British League championship title
Oxford United football club relocated their home ground to the Kassam Stadium near Blackbird Leys.
